and it is property of the Most High like maaser. Above, 3:17.
unless he gave it as unripe fruit. Before it reached the season of the tithes (Peirush HaMishnayot, Maaser Sheni 5:5).
if he wished, he redeems it as wine, and likewise olives. Since wine and oil are important liquids, and grapes and olives are meant for pressing.
one does not change them from their natural state. One does not press them (as above, 3:11, regarding maaser sheni).
a vineyard of the fourth year. And the same applies to other fruit ("neta revai").
has no forgotten sheaf etc.. Since it is property of the Most High (Peirush HaMishnayot, Maaser Sheni 5:3).
forgotten sheaf. As explained in Hilchot Matnot Aniyim 1:5-6.
peah. Ibid. 1:1-2.
peret. Ibid. 4:15.
olelot. Ibid. 4:17.
that they be brought up to Jerusalem. And not redeemed.
a day's journey in every direction. All grapes that grew within a day's journey of Jerusalem on every side.

in order to adorn the markets of Jerusalem with fruit. For neta revai fruit is abundant (unlike maaser sheni, which is a certain percentage of the crop), and those who go up bring part of the fruit to the market to distribute as a gift (Daat Aharon; and see Yerushalmi, Maaser Sheni 5:2, that before the enactment there was a shortage of grapes in Jerusalem because they are used for libations).
how does one redeem neta revai. In the time of the Temple (and nowadays one redeems even with a perutah and afterwards destroys it, as explained in Hilchot Ma'akhalot Assurot 10:17).

he places the basket before three. He places a basket of fruit before three people who are expert in appraisal (Rik"u, Arukh HaShulchan 135:12; and see above, 4:20, that with maaser sheni they required three only when the value is not known, but here they required three always because the value of the expenses must be assessed).

how much would a person be willing to redeem it for a sela on condition that etc.. How many baskets of fruit are worth a sela, taking into account that the buyer must spend from his own money the costs of guarding, gathering the fruit ("the workers"), and transport ("the donkey-drivers").
for they estimate the price. They assess the price.
from the price of so many baskets for a sela. According to a price of so many baskets per sela.
neither guards nor workers. For the orchards are ownerless, and every person picks a little for his house (Hilchot Shemittah 4:24).
he has only the wage of gathering alone. Only the expense of gathering the fruit is deducted.
for everyone's hand is equal. For anyone may pick.
to mark it with clods of earth. To mark it with lumps of soil (Peirush HaMishnayot, Maaser Sheni 5:1).
with potsherd. Fired clay (ibid.).
and those who are modest. Those who are scrupulous.

all that is gathered etc.. Everything that will be gathered is subject to redemption at the time of its gathering (Radbaz), or they would say this every evening over what was gathered during the day (Daat Aharon).
as we explained. Above, 5:2.

on the first of Tishrei... and from when do they count etc.. The counting of the tree's years begins from the time of its planting, and the subsequent years of its count begin on the first of Tishrei, as below.
and he does not count from Rosh Hashanah to Rosh Hashanah. One who plants in the middle of the year need not wait until Rosh Hashanah to begin counting.
until the planting takes hold. Until its roots spread in the ground (Peirush HaMishnayot, Shevi'it 2:6).
an ordinary taking hold. The usual time of taking hold.
two weeks. Two weeks.
forty-four days. Fourteen days for taking hold, and thirty days more that count as a year.
a year has been counted for him. And at the Rosh Hashanah following his planting, the second year begins.
even though they ripened after several days. Although the fruit finished ripening after the years of orlah passed, it has the law of orlah.

and if the year was made a leap year, it was made a leap year for the fourth year or for orlah. That the year of orlah or of the fourth year becomes longer, since the count is by years and not by months, so a leap year is like any other year.

and it is neta revai from Rosh Hashanah. When the time of planting is after the fifteenth of Av, the years of orlah end on Rosh Hashanah and he need not wait until the fifteenth of Shevat of the fourth year, since this waiting is needed only in a case where we were lenient with him in the first year (for example, if he planted before the fifteenth of Av).
three years from day to day. For example, if he planted on Rosh Chodesh Kislev, the fruit is orlah until Rosh Chodesh Kislev three years later.

and I have seen the Geonim etc.. The commentators on the Rambam wrote that he refers to what is brought in Sefer Halakhot Gedolot (Hilchot Orlah, no. 6), that one should not eat neta revai fruit that has been redeemed until the fifth year arrives (see also Hilchot Ma'akhalot Assurot 10:18).
the leaves. Of all trees.
and the tender shoots. The blossoms at the tips of branches while still soft (Peirush HaMishnayot, Orlah 1:7).
and vine waters. Water that came out of a cut vine branch (ibid.).
and the semadar. The bud (blossom) of the vine, from which the grape grows (ibid.).
are permitted in orlah and in the fourth year. Since they are not fruit (and the laws of orlah and the fourth year were stated regarding fruit; see Leviticus 19:23-24).
